market_summary: US equities closed mixed on Tuesday, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average surging over 500 points (+1.3%) as investors rotated out of mega-cap technology and into cyclical and value names, while the Nasdaq Composite fell more than 1% and the Nasdaq-100 entered correction territory. The divergence was driven by a deepening selloff in semiconductor and AI-related stocks, triggered by escalating China chip fears and growing scrutiny of Big Tech's massive AI capital spending ahead of key earnings from Microsoft, Meta, and Amazon. Falling oil prices on hopes of de-escalation in the Middle East provided a tailwind for consumer and industrial stocks, while the broader market awaits the Fed's July policy decision and a critical wave of tech earnings.
macro_summary: Rotational Correction Within a Broader Bull Market The market is in a rotational correction phase where AI/tech leadership is being challenged, but the broader economy and earnings remain supportive. The key question is whether the rotation is a healthy broadening or a precursor to a deeper drawdown if mega-cap earnings disappoint. Today's market reflects a violent but orderly rotation out of the most crowded, high-valuation AI and tech trades into value, cyclical, and defensive sectors. This is not a broad market collapse but a repricing of risk premiums within tech, driven by rising skepticism about AI capex returns and China supply chain risks. The macro backdrop of falling oil, stable rates, and decent non-tech earnings supports the rotation narrative. The macro backdrop is defined by a tug-of-war between easing inflation and geopolitical risks on one hand, and rising uncertainty about AI investment returns and China tech decoupling on the other. Falling oil prices and declining bond yields suggest the market is pricing in a less hawkish Fed, but the violent rotation out of tech indicates that investors are demanding higher risk premiums for AI-exposed names. The Fed's July decision and the BOJ's policy move this week will be critical in determining whether the rotation has legs or is a temporary repositioning ahead of earnings.
risk_summary: Risk appetite is highly polarized. The CBOE Volatility Index (VIX) remained elevated around 22, reflecting ongoing anxiety, but the VIX term structure is in contango, suggesting the market sees the current volatility as event-driven rather than systemic. Breadth was positive on the NYSE but deeply negative on the Nasdaq, confirming the narrowness of the selloff. Bond inflows have surged as investors seek safety, but credit spreads remain relatively stable, indicating no broad stress. Sentiment is cautious but not panicked, with the focus squarely on mega-cap earnings and the Fed.

top_events.title: Dow surges 500+ points on value rotation, falling oil
top_events.summary: The Dow Jones Industrial Average surged over 500 points (+1.3%) as investors rotated out of mega-cap tech and into value and cyclical stocks. Falling oil prices on hopes of US-Iran de-escalation provided a tailwind for consumer, industrial, and transportation stocks.

top_events.title: Oil prices plunge on US-Iran de-escalation hopes
top_events.summary: Crude oil prices fell over 4% on hopes of a de-escalation between the US and Iran, with reports of 'good talks' regarding the Strait of Hormuz. The drop in oil provided a major tailwind for consumer and industrial stocks.

top_events.title: Nasdaq-100 enters correction territory as semiconductor stocks plunge
top_events.summary: The Nasdaq-100 fell over 1% and officially entered correction territory, down more than 10% from its recent high, as the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index plunged over 4%. The selloff was driven by escalating China chip fears and growing investor skepticism about AI spending returns.

top_events.title: Asian Stocks Eye Gains as Oil Offsets Chip Selloff: Markets Wrap
top_events.summary: Asian equity markets are poised for a positive open as a sharp decline in oil prices counterbalances ongoing weakness in semiconductor stocks, suggesting a rotation trade is taking hold.

top_events.title: SK Hynix profit surges 557% but misses estimates, chip selloff deepens
top_events.summary: SK Hynix reported a 557% surge in second-quarter profit to a new high, but the results missed analyst estimates. The miss, combined with broader China chip fears, deepened the selloff in memory and semiconductor stocks globally.

top_events.title: Apple Overtakes Nvidia—Which Will Be Bigger by End of July?
top_events.summary: Apple has surpassed Nvidia in market capitalization, sparking debate over which mega-cap tech stock will lead by month-end amid shifting AI narratives.

top_events.title: New York Gold, Bonds, and Dollar: 'Oil Price Drop vs. Tightening Concerns'... Dollar, Interest Rates, and Gold Prices Decline Together
top_events.summary: A simultaneous decline in the dollar, Treasury yields, and gold prices suggests the market is pricing in both deflationary oil shocks and potential central bank tightening.

top_events.title: S&P 500 rises as oil drop outweighs chip selloff
top_events.summary: The S&P 500 managed to close higher as a steep decline in oil prices offset a significant selloff in semiconductor stocks.

sector_summary: Positive sectors/themes: Consumer Staples (Coca-Cola beat, defensive rotation), Industrials (falling oil, Ford guidance, value rotation), Transportation (lower fuel costs, UPS beat), Healthcare (defensive bid, rate sensitivity); Negative sectors/themes: Semiconductors (China fears, AI capex scrutiny, correction), Mega-cap Tech & AI (rotation out, capex concerns), Space & Defense (SpaceX losses, peak defense spending fears), Energy (falling oil prices on geopolitical hopes); Themes to watch: Value vs. Growth Rotation: Is this a tactical shift or the start of a sustained regime change?, AI Monetization Reality Check: Can Microsoft, Meta, and Amazon justify their capex with revenue growth?, China Decoupling & Chip Supply Chain: How far will export controls go and what is the impact on global tech?, Geopolitical Detente & Commodity Prices: Will US-Iran talks lead to a sustained drop in oil and a broader risk-on move?
